_fixture: Synthetic example for UI development; not real data. Six 30-minute points from one evening peak.

algorithm.description: Day-ahead imbalance price from linear trend, half-hourly seasonal dummies, daily Fourier terms and GB-clock calendar (daily and weekly) regressions, scored by a rolling-origin backtest.

tables.metrics: Scores per model, pooled over the ok folds; MASE, RMSSE and MSIS averaged per fold
tables.by_horizon: MAE, RMSE and 80%/95% coverage per model and lead step
tables.folds: Every forecast origin per model with its status; excluded folds carry a message

algorithm.limitations: Only calendar follows the Europe/London clock, so it alone is exact on 46- and 50-period days; the others count elapsed half-hours. Point forecasts only are stored. Out-of-sample: each forecast uses only prices settled before its origin, and every model is refitted at every origin. Origins step by elapsed half-hours, so they shift by an hour of local time across a clock change. Intervals are model-based; WMAPE and sMAPE are fractions. A fold with a missing price in its window or targets is excluded, not imputed. Not a probability of a price spike or a trading signal.

param_descriptions.horizon: Periods forecast from each origin, which is also the step between origins (48 = one day ahead, once a day)
param_descriptions.window: Settled periods each fit uses, ending at the origin; at most 1344 (28 days)
param_descriptions.max_folds: Most origins a run may use; a longer range fails instead of running for hours (60 = about 60 days at horizon 48)
param_descriptions.season_length: Seasonal period in half-hours used to scale MASE, RMSSE and MSIS (48 = daily)
param_descriptions.models: Settings of each model; the names match the output prefixes and the model column of the tables
